newsitem.title: RUSSIA: CSFB buys $120 mln Russian Tatarstan bond issue.
newsitem.headline: CSFB buys $120 mln Russian Tatarstan bond issue.

text.p: The Russian autonomous republic of Tatarstan has issued 700 billion roubles ($120 million) of fixed coupon bearing short-term bonds (RKO), CS First Boston said in a statement on Tuesday.
Credit Suisse First Boston (Cyprus) Ltd. bought the entire issue, consisting of an 18 month tranche and a two-year tranche, each with a 20 percent coupon payable semi-annually, it said.

CSFB said trade in the bonds would begin in the first week of July on the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX), where the bonds are registered and which is the depository and settlement center for them.
CSFB acted as a paying agent for the bonds issued in a closed subscription on June 16 and as a co-adviser to the issuer.
Tatarstan, located in southern European Russia, has large oil reserves and is one of the best-known regional bond issuers.

An issue prospectus for two tranches of 320 billion and 380 billion roubles maturing on December 10, 1998 and June 10, 1999, respectively, was registered by the Ministry of Finance of Russia on June 6.
The first interest payment for both tranches of the paperless state securities with one million rouble nominal value is due on December 10, 1997.
